decisions.question: Do all 14 launchable harnesses preserve single-token prompt argv separation across 28 branches?
Are launchable harnesses (14), account providers (3), and usage collectors (4) 1-to-1 isomorphic?
What share of Omarchy's 16 agent safety controls are hard OS/code boundaries vs soft conventions?
decisions.closest_label: 0/14 OS sandbox in omarchy-agent; 12/14 pass auto/bypass flags

callouts.lead: Omarchy integrates agents at the OS session/launcher/telemetry layer rather than building a proprietary agent runtime.
callouts.body: All 28 launcher paths preserve single-argument prompt boundaries, but 12/14 unprompted branches pass permission-bypass flags (--yolo, --allow-all, bypassPermissions) without an OS-level container sandbox.

cards.headline: 6 mechanism tracks, 12 formal contract checks
cards.subtitle: Each check compares an explicit architectural expectation or documentation claim against fixed source lines in omacom/omarchy@9480d1b. Misses (✕) mark verified contract drift or soft-boundary hazards.

rows.question: Attachment harness list (13) vs bin/omarchy-agent case branches (14)
Single-argument prompt boundary across 14 harnesses × 2 modes (28 paths)
Unattended/bypass flag retention from unprompted to prompted mode (12 harnesses)
Idempotent skill symlink provisioning across global harness roots (omarchy-provision-user)
Symlink target namespace coverage across all 14 launchable harnesses
rows.decider_answer: 6/14 linked (8 harnesses have no symlink root)

rows.question: Pre-notification filter gates (_UID, disabled, ignore, mute, seen_key) + click gate
Provider set isomorphism across launcher (14), accounts (3), and usage (4)
Autoswitch invariants: mode=auto, >=95% trigger, exclude Waiting for auth, 5h->wk->num
Candidate ranking exclusion when cached account usage has stale=true
shell/plugins/agents/README.md claim that QML plugin is 'strictly a display layer'
Headless test/all (11 shell suites) vs graphical VM test/acceptance (1 suite) split
Hard deterministic OS/code boundaries vs soft conventions across 16 controls
rows.decider_answer: 5/16 hard boundaries (0/14 OS sandbox in launcher)

callouts.lead: 5 of 12 contract checks passed 100% as hard invariants (Auto); 7 of 12 exposed critical architectural boundaries (Confirm / Human).
callouts.body: Hard invariants hold on argv boundary preservation (28/28), 6-root skill symlinks (6/6), 5-stage crash filtering + click gate (5/5), 95% autoswitch rules (4/4), and headless vs VM test separation (11/11).

callouts.lead: Why the 7 ✕ boundary flags matter for engineering reuse.
callouts.body: crush drops --yolo in prompted mode (91.7%); 8 of 14 harnesses have no global skill symlink root (42.9%); autoswitch does not filter stale=true caches (0%); and ~/Work + prompt rules are soft conventions, not an OS sandbox (31.3% hard).

cards.headline: From journald coredump to argv-safe agent launch
cards.subtitle: How Omarchy bridges systemd-coredump JSON events, D-Bus notification actions, and provider-pinned CLI execution without shell-evaluating untrusted crash metadata.
cards.top_code:
{
  "SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER": "systemd-coredump",
  "_UID": "1000",
  "COREDUMP_EXE": "/usr/bin/waybar",
  "COREDUMP_UNIT": "waybar.service",
  "COREDUMP_SIGNAL": "11",
  "COREDUMP_SIGNAL_NAME": "SIGSEGV",
  "COREDUMP_TIMESTAMP": "1787843905000000"
}
# omarchy-crash-watch packs NUL-delimited execArgv -> D-Bus ActionInvoked click required
cards.transition: ↓ user clicks 'Investigate with AI' -> omarchy-agent-crash builds prompt & omarchy-launch-agent pins provider home
cards.bottom_code:
<crash_investigation_prompt>
Application: /usr/bin/waybar (waybar.service) · Signal: 11 (SIGSEGV)
Step 1: coredumpctl info 1787843905000000 + journalctl --since/@timestamp
Step 2: Identify root cause (config vs package update vs upstream bug)
Step 3: Propose fix and ask for confirmation before modifying files
</crash_investigation_prompt>
# omarchy-agent-account-exec claude -> exports OMARCHY_AGENT_CLAUDE_HOME & CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
# exec $1 "$@" -> claude --dangerously-skip-permissions "<prompt>" -> <answer>

callouts.lead: Hard argv boundary up to CLI entry, followed by high-privilege CLI execution.
callouts.body: Crash fields never pass through bash eval; notification-daemon invokes execArgv directly. However, once launched, the default harness receives --dangerously-skip-permissions / --yolo inside ~/Work, relying on prompt instructions to pause before edits.

callouts.lead: Argv safety and explicit environment overrides held at 100.0% (0.0 pts drift), while collector failure fallback dropped -25.0 pts.
callouts.body: Explicit CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME / GROK_HOME overrides cleanly bypass session pinning (100%). Under network failure, Claude (900s) and Grok (30d refresh) retain cached limits, whereas Codex clears limits and Fireworks is stateless.

cards.headline: Batched static contract verification vs one-by-one
cards.subtitle: Shared in-memory blob SHA-1 + line-range table verification across 87 cited files (1, 3, 6, and 12 check cohorts) vs per-question process invocation.

callouts.lead: 12 contract cohorts batched took 137 ms vs 1,848 ms one by one (13.5x faster).
callouts.body: Medians of 7 measured local runs on Windows ARM64 (CPython 3.12.10) over 87 SHA-verified git blobs. Upstream runtime polling timers (not run): 15s Claude probe, 20s scan cache, 30s retryAdvised, 60s Grok probe, 180s near-limit, 900s default.

cards.headline: Where Omarchy's agent design shines, and where not to copy it
good_fit: Single-user developer desktop unifying 14 heterogeneous agent CLIs behind one hotkey/terminal contract
Single-source-of-truth SKILL.md distribution via idempotent symlinks across multi-vendor agent directories
Human-in-the-loop OS crash triage: systemd-coredump filtering + notification click -> structured diagnostic prompt
Local multi-subscription quota pooling (95% threshold autoswitch + per-process credential home pinning)
Separating fast headless shell contract tests (test/all) from VM-only desktop acceptance tests
not_for: Multi-tenant or enterprise zero-trust environments requiring mandatory OS container/VM sandboxing
Treating ~/Work directory cd, --yolo flags, or SKILL.md 'ask before editing' text as a security boundary
Using local transcript token estimates or undocumented web/OAuth usage endpoints as authoritative billing
Assuming symlinked SKILL.md files are identically discovered and enforced by every third-party CLI
